messages:
maya (product): Quick follow-up from the GTM/customer sync — we need a concrete prioritization for the embeddings endpoint (dims, batch limits, model fallback, response shape) so we can lock Q2 launch scope. Key asks: enterprise customers want 4096 dims and per-request batching up to ~2048 vectors. Also a low-latency single-vector path for search use cases.

ben (eng-platform): Agree we need to pick a minimal viable contract. Big tradeoffs: big dims + huge batches blow up GPU mem and tail latency. For hosted API I'd prefer to limit public dims to 2048 and recommend Dedicated for 4096. Can we do a gated rollout? @sophie thoughts on perf?

sophie (eng-ml): Perf notes: 4096 dims increases KV cache + attention costs. For reference, measurements: 1536 dim single-vector 95p ~ 70ms; 4096 single-vector 95p ~ 200ms on our A100 config (no batching). Batching 512x4096 -> OOM unless we quantize aggressively. Options: 1) support 4096 only on Dedicated; 2) allow 4096 in hosted but limit batch_size<=8; 3) provide downsampled 2048 route.

ryan (infra): Capacity angle: if we allow host-side 2048+ batch windows we need extra slots and burst pool. Autoscaler needs new heuristics for vector-heavy queues. Also need circuit breaker for memory spikes.

carlos (sales): Customer piece: Large retail customer will only go to prod if 4096 dims and batch 1024 in a single request (for nightly embedding ingest). They are open to Dedicated but want a plan and timeline. They asked for launch SLA and an intermediate compatibility mode so their pipeline can start integrating.

maya (product): Proposal: ship MVP hosted endpoint supporting dims=[64,128,512,1536,2048] with batch_size limit 1024 for small dims (<=1536) and batch_size limit 64 for dims>1536. Offer Dedicated with explicit 4096 support and batch up to 2048. Launch criteria: docs + SDKs, perf tests (95p latency targets), one pilot customer on Dedicated, backward-compatible response shape.

sophie (eng-ml): For model selection/fallback: default model = "redwood-embed-1" (2048), large model = "redwood-embed-large-4096" (Dedicated). Implement automatic fallback policy: if requested dims incompatible, return 400 with guidance OR map to nearest supported dims with a warning header. Also add an option to request "downsample": true to convert 4096 -> 2048 server-side (lossy but fast).

ben (eng-platform): API response format suggestion (minimal change from current):
```
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-1",
  "dimensions": 2048,
  "embeddings": [[...], [...]],
  "meta": {"requested_dimensions": 4096, "downsampled": true} 
}
```
This keeps outer shape consistent and lets clients detect downsampling via meta.

maya (product): Launch checklist items I care about: 1) Perf benchmarks for each dim/batch combo (suites + public doc), 2) SDK changes + migration guide for downsample path, 3) Pricing signal for large dims (to cover infra costs), 4) Pilot with retail customer on Dedicated by end of Q2.

ryan (infra): I'll add autoscale rules + memory circuit-breaker. Need owners: @ben for API contract + error codes, @sophie for perf budgets, @ryan for infra runbooks, @maya for customer comms.

ben (eng-platform): Sounds good. I'll draft API contract and error codes this week. Will include explicit 400 payload example and a 202+async ingest option for very large batches.

carlos (sales): :thumbsup: I’ll relay the Dedicated pilot timeline and push for an LOE for their infra team. Appreciate the downsample opt — that helps them unblock.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: feature/embeddings-dims-prio -> staging at 2024-06-05T14:00Z (dry-run).

maya (product): Thanks all — next sync Friday to review perf numbers and the API draft. If anyone objects to the proposal above, speak now or DM. :ear:
